sources: Gwynn, Edward. The Metrical Dindshenchas. Royal Irish Academy, Todd Lecture Series. Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, and Co., Ltd. 1906–1924. Reprinted Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies, School of Celtic Studies, 1991, Part 4, pp. 3–9.

text: Ruad is an Irish maiden goddess. The well-known falls of Assaroe may owe their name to her. She reached Ireland from the Otherworld aboard Abcán's boat, whose hull was bronze and whose sail was tin. Her stay in Ireland proved short. She met her end at the waterfall after mermaids sang from Abcán's boat and drew her into the whirling water. In another tale, Abcán was caught by the hero Cúchulainn of Ulster. He set himself free by playing lullabies so strong that the warrior fell asleep. Abcán shared much with the dwarf musician Fer Í, and the pair may be related.

okr.objective: Present Ruad as the maiden who may have given the waterfall of Assaroe its name.
